Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency reporting and the routing controls. Finance asked me to confirm a few procurement constraints before we finalize the commercial terms:

- We need each invoice to map to a ClearPath legal entity and a single PO number per legal entity (we operate three billing entities).
- Line items on the invoice must include the SKU and subscription start/end dates for reconciliation with our ERP.
- Preferred cadence is monthly invoicing with net60 payment terms.
- Discounts must be reflected on the invoice lines and tied to committed spend thresholds (we can only accept discounts that apply after the monthly committed threshold is hit).

Can Redwood support attaching multiple entity PO numbers if we roll up a single consolidated invoice, or do you require separate invoices per PO? Also, are discounts applied pro-rata across months or only after the commit is reached?

I attached our standard PO template for reference (Enterprise_PO_Template_v2.pdf).

If you need a short call with procurement/finance to iron this out, we can schedule one.

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear summary and for the PO template. Looping in Vanessa and Karthik from billing to confirm mechanics. A few quick answers and open items from our side:

- Separate invoice per legal entity: Redwood's billing platform can emit separate invoices per legal entity/PO number. We can also produce a consolidated statement that lists each invoice and PO if you prefer a rollup for accounting — the invoices themselves would still be per-entity for ERP matching.

- SKU + dates: we can include SKU, subscription start/end, and subscription_id on each invoice line so your ERP can match.

- Monthly cadence & net60: standard hosted customers are on net45. Net60 is possible but requires approval from Finance for this deal size and a credit check. Vanessa / Karthik — can you advise on net60 approval for DEAL-8421-CPH?

- Discount ladder: Redwood applies discounts at invoice level based on cumulative committed spend buckets in the contract. Our typical behavior is: if the monthly committed threshold is not met, invoices show the non-discounted price; once cumulative committed spend crosses a threshold, discounts are applied prospectively. We can discuss a pro-rata approach, but that is an exception.

Proposed next steps:
1) Vanessa/Karthik to confirm net60 feasibility and whether we can offer pro-rata discounts for partial-month thresholds.
2) If net60 needs additional approvals, we can propose net45 with a one-time credit to bridge the difference for first quarter while approvals finish.
3) Quick call with ClearPath procurement later this week to align on PO/ERP mapping and confirm the final invoice format.

I've attached our Pricing_Bucket_Matrix.xlsx which maps buckets to invoice line descriptions.

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart

Evelyn,

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from procurement/finance here:

- We cannot accept consolidated invoices that do not map to PO numbers — each invoice must have the PO in a distinct header so our AP system can automatically route and approve. A consolidated statement is fine as long as it is an accompanying document, not the primary invoice.

- Regarding discounts: our committed spend is defined per legal entity. If one entity hits a higher bucket and others do not, the discount should only apply to the line items tied to that entity's PO. We need per-entity bucket calculation rather than a company-wide aggregate.

- Net60 is non-negotiable for our treasury team for this contract unless Redwood provides a milestone-based payment schedule or performance-backed holdback. If you can do net45 + a 15-day payer-side holdback that releases after quarterly health checks, that might be a workable alternative.

We're happy to set a 30-minute call with our AP/ERP analyst and procurement to go through the invoice sample you mentioned. Available windows: Thu 11/12 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri 11/13 09:00-10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Alex
